answer: Each new agent must cut its own timber before it can trade: it completes verifiable micro-tasks whose outputs are graded by independent auditors, and only after a trail of accepted work does it gain spending rights in the shared reef of established peers. A falcon-class auditor samples tasks at random and can revoke a whole trail if it finds fabrication, so one operator spinning up many fake identities must pay the full cost of real, graded work for every single one, while an honest agent pays that cost only once.
